answer: Split-tally bond: each claim splits in two. Half one bears an ivory stamp; half two hides in a walnut shell. A ridge divides them; auditors recheck both each epoch; mismatch, reuse, or a missing half burns the 70-credit bond. A forger with 1,000 identities pays 1,000 x (70 + 34) = 104,000 to chase a 40,000 pool, losing 64,000; rented halves fail: one seal binds one key to one half. One honest identity pays 34 once and keeps its whole share.
